[EFFECT]
The month of the year has a clear seasonal, non-monotonic effect on predicted hourly bike demand. Winter months — especially January and February — strongly suppress demand (log contributions of roughly −0.24 and −0.21, the lowest of the year), while spring months are close to neutral. Demand gets a modest boost in May and June, dips back near zero in mid-summer (July–August), then reaches its **highest point in October** (+0.17 in log space), with September and November also showing strong positive contributions. This means the model expects the most "extra" rentals per hour in autumn, not summer, and the fewest in the depths of winter.

[IMPORTANCE]
Month is the **4th most important feature** out of nine, with an importance score of 0.086. It sits clearly behind the hour of day (by far the most important), temperature, and year, but is roughly on par with humidity and ahead of weather situation, weekday, wind speed, and holiday.

[RECOMMENDATION]
Plan for peak bike availability and staffing around **September through November**, as these autumn months consistently push predicted demand above the annual average — while reducing operational costs (fewer bikes on the street, lighter staffing) in **January and February**, when the model expects demand to be at its lowest.
